planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Regal Red is a Japanese painted fern selection bred for unusually deep, saturated burgundy-red coloring in the fronds and stems.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Regal Red is a Japanese painted fern cultivar selected for exceptionally deep, saturated wine-red to burgundy coloring through the fronds and stems, a stronger and more uniform red than the more common silver-and-maroon blend of the classic species. The rich color intensifies with some morning sun and holds well through the season in reliably moist shade. Like other Japanese painted ferns, it combines beautifully with hostas, heucheras, and brunnera in a mixed shade border, its dark coloring providing dramatic contrast against chartreuse or silver-leaved companions. Consistent moisture is essential, since painted ferns scorch and go dormant early in dry shade. Cut back old fronds in late winter before new growth emerges, and divide congested clumps in early spring every three to four years to maintain vigor and color intensity.

common_name: Divisilobum Soft Shield Fern (Finely Dissected Fern)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Divisilobum is a finely dissected soft shield fern selection with lacy, feathery, evergreen fronds.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Divisilobum is a soft shield fern selection with exceptionally finely cut, lacy, almost feathery fronds, among the most delicate-looking textures of any hardy evergreen fern, though the foliage is actually quite tough and weather-resistant. The arching, evergreen fronds hold their good looks through much of the winter in milder climates, providing structure and texture in the shade garden even in the off season. Its refined, dissected texture contrasts beautifully with the broad leaves of hostas or heucheras and pairs well with other ferns of contrasting form. More tolerant of dry shade than many ferns once established, though it still performs best with consistent moisture and a humus-rich soil that mimics its native woodland floor habitat. Remove tattered old fronds in late winter just before new growth (fiddleheads) emerges, and divide congested clumps in spring every few years.
